reviews: Fresh rice paper rolls packed with herbs and a clear, fragrant pho broth. Light, clean, and lunch came in under ten bucks.
They keep peanuts out of the kitchen entirely, and nothing is made with milk, cream or butter. My friend with the allergy and my lactose-sensitive coworker both ate without a worry.
Crisp herb salads and fresh summer rolls, all light and cheap. Nothing creamy or buttery on the whole menu.
Peanuts are the star here: every plate comes with their peanut dipping sauce, and crushed peanuts go on top of nearly everything. Delicious if nuts are your thing.
Fresh, light bowls loaded with herbs, and cheap for downtown. The staff told me there are no peanuts anywhere in the kitchen.

Dairy runs through the mains, not just the iced coffee: butter-garlic noodles, curries finished with cow's milk and cream, condensed milk stirred into the sauces. Hard to order around it if milk doesn't agree with you.
Deep-fried spring rolls, oily stir-fries and everything glistening with grease. Cheap and filling, but I needed a nap after.
No peanuts in the kitchen and they cook without milk or butter, so it's easy on allergies. Just don't come here looking for anything light.
Clean, simple sushi and fresh cucumber and avocado rolls. Light, cheap, and a nice break from the usual noodle spots.
Peanut-safe kitchen and no milk or cream in anything. Strictly sushi and sashimi, though, so don't come in craving pho.
